act: Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (Union law — Art. 62(a), pre-amendment)

source.ref: Indian Stamp Act, 1899, Sch. I Art. 62(a) + S.O. 130(E) dated 28-1-2004 (as corrected by S.O. 522(E) dated 7-4-2005)
source.quoted_text: Central Sch. I Art. 62 (both columns, Delhi-Revenue-hosted text): 'TRANSFER (whether with or without consideration) — (a) of shares in an incorporated company or other body corporate — [Twenty-five paise] for hundred rupees or part thereof of the value of the share' [rate as substituted by S.O. 130(E) w.e.f. 1-3-2004] = 0.25% of the value. Rounding proviso from the same 2004 order: 'The duty chargeable shall, wherever necessary, be rounded off to the next five paise.' This pre-amendment regime governs physical transfers executed BEFORE 1 July 2020.

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: HIGH (article text + 2004 order both in the committed source PDF). Historical version for Flow D / as-of computations. Base: value of the share (consideration; for no-consideration transfers the pre-2020 base was the share VALUE — flag for adjudication-mode inputs). The ceil-to-5-paise rounding is the Q6 micro-exception, encoded ONLY here.

act: Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (Union law — Part AA / s.9A-9B uniform regime)

source.ref: Finance Act 2019 (Part I, Ch. IV) amendments to the Indian Stamp Act + MoF notifications dated 10-12-2019 and 30-03-2020 (regime effective 1-7-2020)
source.quoted_text: Founder ruling (Q4, 2026-07-16): 'Physical share transfers on Form SH-4 attract stamp duty at 0.015% of consideration under Article 62 of the Indian Stamp Act as amended, uniform across India — effective 1 July 2020 via the Finance Act 2019 amendments and MoF notifications of 10 December 2019 and 30 March 2020; no state deviation is permitted; documents still citing 0.25% are outdated.' Per the DEA FAQs on the amended Act, off-market transfers WITHOUT consideration (gifts) attract nil duty, since the base is consideration.
